payload.reason: The evidence provides insights into how variance is calculated in relation to model outputs, particularly through the Expected Gradient Length (EGL) method, which is linked to variance reduction in estimators.

claims.text: Expected Gradient Length (EGL) is used to reduce variance in model outputs by selecting instances that lead to significant changes in model parameters, thus minimizing expected variance over the test set.
EGL computes the expectation of the gradient norm over possible labelings, which helps in understanding the variance associated with model predictions.
